newsitem.title: JAPAN: IMF sees new standby loans for Pakistan this year.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees new standby loans for Pakistan this year.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund is aiming to reach a new standby loan agreement with the new Pakistani government later this year, IMF Deputy Managing Director Stanley Fischer said.

"We will be working with them towards a new standby rather than renewing the old one. Somewhere later this year would be the aim," Fischer told Reuters Financial Television in an interview broadcast on Wednesday.
Fischer said Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's three-month-old government is the country's strongest government in many years, and its economic reforms have a very good chance of working.

"But the politics in Pakistan are quite complicated," he said. "I think that if they get everything done that they would like to get done and that they've agreed to with us, there's a very good chance of it working."
He said the government had laid out a "pretty ambitious" set of structural reform measures, which it planned to push through very rapidly.
"They want to move less drastically on the macro side," he added.
Pakistan's inability to meet agreed economic targets prompted the IMF to halt a standby loan after Sharif took power in his February election triumph.
An IMF mission arrived in Islamabad last week to set broad macroeconomic targets for 1997/98 in consultation with Finance Ministry officials who are preparing the June 14 budget.
Fischer is in Tokyo to attend a two-day conference on macro-economic adjustment and economic growth.
